title: Spellings from Greek, French and Latin
keyIdea: English borrowed many words from Greek, French and Latin, and some kept the spelling habits of their first language. In Greek words the /k/ sound is often spelt ch, as in chorus, chemist and echo. In French words the /sh/ sound is often spelt ch, as in chef and machine, and a /g/ or /k/ sound at the end can be spelt gue or que, as in league and unique, with a silent u and e. In Latin words sc can say /s/, as in science and scene, but only when the next letter is e, i or y. Saying the word, then asking which pattern fits, turns a guess into a choice.
familyTip: Keep a three-column list on the fridge: Greek ch (k), French ch (sh) and French gue or que. When one of you spots a new word, such as orchestra, parachute or antique, say it aloud together and add it to the right column.

visual.caption: Which sound does ch make? Drag each word, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort ch words by sound, build Greek and French spellings, finish -gue and -que endings, test the sc rule and proofread.

kid: Lots of English words came from other languages. Some still use the spelling from back then. If you know where a word came from, you can spell it.
In words from Greek, the sound k is often spelt ch. Think of chorus, echo and chemist. In words from French, the sound sh is often spelt ch. Think of chef and machine.
Some French words end with gue or que. League ends with a g sound. Unique ends with a k sound. You do not hear the u and e, but you still write them.
Words from Latin can have sc, like science and scene. Here sc says s. Look at the next letter. If it is e, i or y, sc says s. If it is a, o or u, sc says sk, like in scarf.
adult: Ages 8 to 10. English Appendix 1 of the national curriculum in England lists four patterns of foreign origin for Years 3 and 4: /k/ spelt ch (Greek: scheme, chorus, chemist, echo, character), /ʃ/ spelt ch (mostly French: chef, chalet, machine, brochure), /g/ spelt -gue and /k/ spelt -que (French: league, tongue, antique, unique) and /s/ spelt sc (Latin: science, scene, discipline, fascinate, crescent). Pupils use and extend them through Years 5 and 6.

The idea that ties these together is that the sound alone does not settle the spelling. The word's history does. Children learn to say the word, notice that ch is not making the chip sound, and ask which family the word belongs to. The sc rule is the same soft c rule as in city and cent: c before e, i or y says /s/, so the c in sc is silent there.

Common mistakes: writing the sound the plain English way, as in kemist, korus, shef or masheen; dropping the silent letters, as in leeg, leage or uneek; leaving out the silent c, as in sience or sene; and assuming sc always says /s/, which fails for scarf, scab and scoop. Some children also over-apply the new patterns and write words like baque for back, so ask whether the word sounds French or Greek before using them.

In the lab your child sorts twelve ch words by sound and builds six Greek and French spellings in a gap. They finish six -gue and -que endings and sort ten sc words by the letter that follows. Then they fix six misspelt words, each written the way it sounds.

practice.prompt: In which word does ch say k?
practice.hint: Say each word aloud. Which ch sounds like the k in kit?
practice.explain: chemist is from Greek, so ch says k. chin has the everyday ch sound, and chef is French, so ch says sh.

practice.prompt: Mia sorts {n} ch words. {g} have a Greek ch that says k. The rest have a French ch that says sh. How many say sh?
practice.hint: Take the Greek words away from all the words.
practice.explain: {n} − {g} = {=n-g} words have a French ch, like chef or machine.

practice.prompt: Which is the right spelling of a sports team group?
practice.hint: It is French. The ending is gue with a silent u and e.
practice.explain: league uses ea for the long e sound and ends gue. leeg and leage drop the silent u and e.

practice.prompt: A list has {a} words ending in gue and {b} words ending in que. How many silent u letters are in those endings?
practice.hint: Each gue or que ending has one silent u.
practice.explain: {a} + {b} = {=a+b}. Every -gue and -que ending has one silent u, and one silent e too.

practice.prompt: In which word does sc say s?
practice.hint: Look at the letter just after sc.
practice.explain: In scene, e comes after sc, so the c is soft and sc says s. In scarf and scoop, a and o come next, so sc says sk.

pool.prompt: Which spelling is right for a machine that washes dishes?
pool.hint: Machine is a French word. How does French spell the sh sound?
pool.explain: machine uses ch for the sh sound and i for the ee sound, the French way.

pool.prompt: Why is the k sound in chorus spelt ch?
choices: Every k sound is spelt ch.
pool.hint: Which language spells k with ch?
pool.explain: chorus came from Greek, and Greek words often spell k with ch. Kit and king do not, so not every k is ch.

pool.prompt: Which word ends with a k sound spelt que?
pool.hint: que says k at the end of some French words.
pool.explain: antique ends que. attack ends ck, the English way, and plague ends gue, which says g.

pool.hint: Keep the silent c, and the vowels are i then e.
pool.explain: science is spelt sc-ie-nce. sience drops the silent c, and scince drops the i.

pool.prompt: A word list has {s} sc words that say s and {k} sc words that say sk. How many sc words are there in all?
pool.hint: Add the s group and the sk group together.
pool.explain: {s} + {k} = {=s+k} sc words. The letter after sc tells you which group each one goes in.

pool.prompt: In which word does ch say sh?
pool.hint: French words spell the sh sound with ch.
pool.explain: brochure is French, so ch says sh. character is Greek, so ch says k, and chair has the everyday ch sound.

pool.prompt: Ben writes uneek. What is the right spelling?
pool.hint: It is French and ends with a k sound.
pool.explain: unique ends que. unick uses the English ck, and uniqe forgets the silent u.

pool.prompt: Why does sc say sk in scarf?
pool.hint: Look at the letter after sc.
pool.explain: After sc comes a, so the c is hard and sc says sk. Before e, i or y, sc says s, as in scene.

pool.prompt: Each French word in a spelling test has {e} silent letters at the end, like the u and e in league. How many silent end letters are in {w} words?
pool.hint: Multiply the silent letters in one word by the number of words.
pool.explain: {w} × {e} = {=w*e} silent letters. You do not hear them, but you write them every time.

pool.prompt: Which word should you spell with ch for the k sound?
pool.explain: echo is Greek, so its k sound is spelt ch. kitten and basket are English words, spelt with k.
